clue.text: Volcanic rock turned up by little creatures

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense, something turned up is flipped over, so the word up is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, then reversed
mice are small animals

explanation.surface: A geologist's find of lava stone dug up by scurrying rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'discovered', but it tells you to flip the word 'up' itself, which then sits in front of the little creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light, porous stone formed from frothy lava, so it is a kind of volcanic rock.

clue.text: One requiring treatment and prepared to wait

blocks.note: first meaning: a person under a doctor's care
second meaning: tolerant of delay

explanation.surface: Someone in a hospital waiting room, needing care and ready to sit it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is a person receiving medical care, and being patient means calmly accepting a delay.

clue.text: Was blue bike seen here?

blocks.note: first meaning: sulked or felt low
second meaning: a small motorised two-wheeler

explanation.surface: Was a blue bicycle spotted in this spot?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like the bike's colour, but it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to be listless and gloomy, so moped is past tense; a moped is also a light motorcycle with pedals.

clue.text: Old TV series about Les? Miserable!

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the name

blocks.note: the American sitcom set in a Boston bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nod to Les Misérables, with the musical's miserable hero in a sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Les? Miserable!' plays on Les Misérables; the punctuation splits name from definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless means gloomy and joyless, the same as miserable.

clue.text: As discs they are unsurpassed

blocks.note: surface reading: vinyl platters that play music
setter's reading: best-ever performances that nobody has beaten

explanation.walkthrough: The one word means both gramophone discs and best-ever performances, so the clue describes both senses at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl album is a record, and an achievement nobody has bettered is also a record, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Payment to author from people in palaces?

blocks.note: first meaning: a share of sales paid to a writer
second meaning: kings, queens and their family

explanation.surface: A writer's earnings coming from the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalty is a fee paid to a creator per copy sold, and royalty also means the monarch's family.

clue.text: Popular holiday destination caught four out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the letters of four rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket report: four batsmen out, caught, at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, much visited by tourists on holiday.

clue.text: Those who keep servants

blocks.note: first meaning: people who retain or keep possession of things
second meaning: long-standing household attendants

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as employers who keep staff; split it after 'keep' to find two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is literally one who retains, and is also a traditional term for a faithful household servant.

clue.text: Clean cake

blocks.note: first meaning: to wipe with a soft absorbent pad
second meaning: a light, airy bake

explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to wash with a soft pad, and a sponge is also a light fluffy cake.

clue.text: Such a flight would be the first for Virgin

definitions.text: Such a flight would be the first

blocks.clueFragment: Such a flight would be the first
blocks.note: first meaning: the inaugural trip of an aircraft
second meaning: an unmarried young woman, untouched

explanation.surface: A new airline route launching for Virgin Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' looks like the airline, but it is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden flight is an aircraft's first, and a maiden is a girl or virgin.

clue.text: End woeful prayer in Irish county

indicators.note: something woeful is in a sorry state, a sign that the letters that follow are a mess to be rearranged

blocks.note: the tip of something is its end
the letters of prayer rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad prayer said at the end of someone's life in rural Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, in the province of Munster.

clue.text: Nine-to-five, say, when allowance is curtailed

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, here meaning the tail letter is chopped off

blocks.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: An office worker's nine-to-five day when the pay allowance is being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine-to-five' suggests working hours, but read as 9:5 it is a proportion between two numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine to five, written 9:5, is an example of a ratio, a comparison between two quantities.

clue.text: Source of berries for community leader

blocks.note: first meaning: a shrub whose dark berries make wine and cordial
second meaning: a senior, respected figure in a church or tribe

explanation.surface: Someone collects berries to hand to the village head.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder tree bears elderberries, and an elder is also a senior person with authority in a community.

clue.text: Old genius transformed pest control treatment

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its shape, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aging mastermind has reinvented the way we deal with vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: Delousing removes lice from a person or animal, which is a treatment to control a pest.

clue.text: Dash back with German article for part-exchange

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the word for dash is read from its end

blocks.note: to dart is to dash quickly
ein is the German for 'a'

explanation.surface: Someone rushes back with a German item to swap at a dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as part payment for a new one, which is what part-exchange means.

clue.text: The inn, as a resort for Greeks

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it asks for the letters to be sorted again into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tavern that serves as a holiday haunt for Greek visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place, but split it as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Athenians are citizens of Athens, the Greek capital, so they are Greeks.

clue.text: Obsequious subordinates close to tears in Arab country

indicators.note: the close of a word is its ending, so only its last letter is wanted
one piece sits inside another word, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: the country at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula
the final letter of tears

explanation.surface: Fawning underlings nearly weeping somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are people who always agree with their boss, i.e. sycophantic underlings.

clue.text: Stand near helter-skelter in Spanish city

indicators.note: helter-skelter means in wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Waiting beside a fairground slide in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A helter-skelter is also a spiral fairground slide, which is the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Santander is a port city on Spain's northern coast, capital of Cantabria.

clue.text: Good landlords providing spirits

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a pub landlord is the host

explanation.surface: Kindly pub landlords serving drinks behind the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Landlords and spirits paint a pub with whisky on the shelves, but the spirits are phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are the spirits of the dead, a second sense of spirits beside strong drink.

clue.text: Weather forecast no longer an issue?

blocks.note: first meaning: a forecaster's word for calm, unchanging weather
second meaning: resolved, decided

explanation.surface: Is the weather forecast no longer something to argue about?
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is an example: a typical word heard in a forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: Forecasters call stable weather settled, and a dispute that is resolved is also settled.

clue.text: Barbara Castle?

definitions.note: the surname of the actress Barbara Windsor

blocks.note: first meaning: Barbara ___, the Carry On and EastEnders actress
second meaning: ___ Castle, the royal home west of London

explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Castle was a Labour cabinet minister, so the clue reads as her name. Instead one surname completes both words: Barbara Windsor, the actress, and Windsor Castle, the royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The same surname fills both gaps: the actress Barbara Windsor and the monarch's home at Windsor Castle.

clue.text: View, finally, that is most extensive

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, so just its closing letter is taken

blocks.note: the final letter of view
id est is the Latin for 'that is', usually shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: A view that, in the end, stretches furthest.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers know 'that is' as IE; here the full Latin id est is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Widest is the superlative of wide, meaning the greatest in extent.

clue.text: Take no comfort in organised riot — ugh!

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: No consolation to be found in a planned disturbance, ugh!
explanation.definitionFit: To rough it is to live without the usual comforts, for example when camping.

clue.text: A group of notes, we hear, producing harmony

indicators.note: hearing points to how the words sound when spoken rather than how they are written

blocks.note: a chord is several notes played together

explanation.surface: A chord that makes a pleasing harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord means agreement or concord, which is harmony in a non-musical sense.

clue.text: Cocky prisoner in the chair, so to speak

indicators.note: speaking a phrase means we go by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: con is short for convict
someone in the chair is seated, and this ending sounds the same

explanation.surface: An arrogant inmate sitting in the chair, almost literally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the chair' could mean chairing a meeting, but here it simply means sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocky and conceited both describe someone with too high an opinion of themselves.

clue.text: Panic, losing head? There's something wrong there

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: terror is extreme fear

explanation.surface: Panic over a mistake once a decapitation is on the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, i.e. something wrong in the place pointed to.

clue.text: Farewell from police officer in a multinational group

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the others, wrapped by them

blocks.note: taken as written
DI is a Detective Inspector
the European Union

explanation.surface: A detective says goodbye on leaving an international body.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French word for goodbye, used in English as a formal farewell.

clue.text: Bury artist after pop's popped off

indicators.note: popping off means leaving, so that word departs from the artist

blocks.note: a painter is an artist
pop and pa are both words for father

explanation.surface: Burying an artist after Dad has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popped off' is slang for died, which fits the burial surface, but it signals removal of pop's letters from the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, which is to bury it.

clue.text: Network's first to plug old tune that's being broadcast

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of network is used
a plug fills a hole, so this letter goes into the gap between the other two pieces

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
the opening letter of network
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A TV channel promoting a golden oldie that is playing now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests advertising, but here it means stopping a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being transmitted live, i.e. currently broadcast.

clue.text: Desperate jockey's final obstacle?

blocks.note: first meaning: a last-gasp attempt when all else has failed
second meaning, read literally: the final ditch jumped in a steeplechase

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as a playful, literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt; literally, it would be the last ditch a horse clears.

clue.text: Section of étude Sir Edward wanted

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from a whole, so the answer is a run of letters within the following words

blocks.note: read straight through the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Elgar wanted a certain passage of a musical study.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on the e is ignored, as accents always are in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired and wanted are synonyms, both past forms of verbs meaning to wish for.

clue.text: Doctor gets Conservative backing to reveal decay

indicators.note: backing implies going backwards, so the word for Conservative runs from its end

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviated title
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A doctor who gets Tory support turns out to be rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as political support, but it tells you to reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that destroys timber in buildings.
